cues.title: 下蹲时先轻后重
cues.caption: 两段都向下，支持力却一小一大。
cues.captionEn: Both stages move down, but support force first falls and then rises.
cues.zh: 站在体重计上缓慢下蹲。开始向下加速时，秤的支持力小于重力，读数变小。接近蹲下的终点，人仍然向下运动，却开始减速，加速度已经朝上，读数反而变大。最后停稳，读数回到原来的值。判断超重还是失重，不能只看人正在向上走还是向下走。
cues.en: Stand on a scale and squat. At first, downward acceleration requires support force smaller than gravity, lowering the reading. Near the bottom, you are still moving down but slowing; acceleration is upward and the reading rises. Once stationary, the original reading returns. Direction of travel alone cannot determine apparent weight.

cues.title: 力平台记录蹲起
cues.titleEn: Record the full squat and rise
cues.caption: 仪器记录支持力；质量与重力未改变。
cues.captionEn: The instrument records support force; mass and gravity do not change.
cues.zh: 把体重计换成力传感器，记录完整的下蹲和站起过程。曲线的虚线是静止时的重力，绿色曲线是支持力。站起时先向上加速，支持力大于重力；接近站稳时向上减速，支持力小于重力。这里的曲线来自一个平滑的示例动作，真实人体的晃动和仪表滤波会让细节不同，但受力关系不变。
cues.en: Replace the scale with a force platform and record a complete squat and rise. The dashed baseline is weight at rest; the green trace is support force. Rising begins with upward acceleration and greater support, then upward braking and smaller support. This smooth example is not a recorded human trial. Real sway and filtering change details but not the force relationship.

cues.title: 电梯上升的三个阶段
cues.titleEn: Three stages of an upward journey
cues.caption: 上升启动偏重，匀速恢复，上升制动偏轻。
cues.captionEn: Heavier at upward start, normal at cruise, lighter while braking.
cues.zh: 现在人保持站立，让电梯完成运动。上升启动时，电梯、人和秤一起向上加速，读数高于静止值。进入匀速段，加速度为零，读数恢复正常，即使电梯仍在上升。制动时加速度向下，读数变小。井道刻线显示运动方向，速度和加速度分开显示，帮助你把三种状态对应到同一条曲线。
cues.en: Keep the passenger standing while the lift moves. At upward start, lift, person and scale accelerate upward together and the reading exceeds its rest value. During constant speed, acceleration is zero and the normal reading returns despite continued ascent. Braking has downward acceleration and a smaller reading. Shaft marks reveal travel, while separate velocity and acceleration readings explain the trace.

cues.title: 换成下降再检验
cues.caption: 下降减速时，加速度向上，仍然超重。
cues.captionEn: A descending lift is heavier while braking upward.
cues.zh: 换成下降过程。启动向下加速，读数变小；匀速下降，读数正常；向下减速时，加速度向上，读数变大。用向上为正方向，支持力减去重力就等于质量乘加速度。体重计上标着千克，是把支持力除以标定的重力加速度后的显示，不代表运动过程中人的真实质量发生变化。
cues.en: Reverse the journey. Downward acceleration lowers the reading; steady descent restores it; downward braking raises it because acceleration points up. With upward positive, support minus weight equals mass times acceleration. A scale labelled in kilograms divides support force by its calibration gravity. That display does not mean the person’s actual mass changes during motion.

cues.title: 静止水瓶为什么漏水
cues.caption: 水面通气，孔口处的压差驱动水流。
cues.captionEn: A vented surface permits a pressure difference that drives the jet.
cues.zh: 在通气的水瓶侧壁开小孔，静止时水会流出。小孔上方的水柱形成压力差，推动水从孔口喷出，再受重力作用沿弯曲路径下落。本例把短时间内的水位变化忽略，先建立静止时的对照。请注意水滴离开瓶子以后已经是独立运动的物体，瓶子的后续动作不会让旧水滴凭空消失。
cues.en: Make a small side hole in a vented bottle. At rest, the water head produces a pressure difference and drives an outward jet, which then curves downward under gravity. Over this short comparison, level change is neglected. Once a droplet leaves, it moves independently: later bottle motion cannot erase water that has already been emitted.

cues.title: 瓶和水一起自由落下
cues.titleEn: Let bottle and water fall together
cues.caption: 持续压差消失；旧水滴仍按原来的速度和重力运动。
cues.captionEn: Sustained pressure vanishes; earlier droplets retain their motion under gravity.
cues.zh: 释放水瓶，瓶和水一起以重力加速度下落。相对于瓶子，维持原来水柱压差的有效重力降为零，持续喷流因而消失。已经喷出的水滴仍继续飞行。这里忽略刚释放时很短的流体惯性过程，所以停止新水流是理想化处理。完全失重说的是支持或压迫作用消失，绝不是地球的引力突然消失。
cues.en: Release the bottle. It and the water accelerate downward at g. Relative to the bottle, effective gravity sustaining the original pressure head becomes zero, so the sustained jet ceases. Earlier droplets keep flying. The brief fluid-inertia transient at release is omitted, so the cutoff is idealized. Complete weightlessness means loss of support or pressure effects, not disappearance of Earth’s gravity.

question.zh: 还在向下蹲，为什么体重计反而变大？
question.en: Why can the scale reading rise while you are still moving down?

lead.zh: 把向下加速和向下减速并排比较，质量与重力始终相同。
lead.en: Compare downward acceleration with downward braking while mass and gravity stay fixed.

principle.zh: 向下减速需要向上的合力，因此支持力大于重力；秤读的是支持力。
principle.en: Braking downward motion requires an upward net force, so support exceeds weight. The scale measures support.

question.zh: 若下蹲到一半停住，读数会保持偏大吗？
question.en: If you stop halfway through the squat, does the reading stay high?

explanation.zh: 停稳后加速度为零，支持力回到mg；蹲得低本身不会改变质量或重力。
explanation.en: Once stationary, acceleration is zero and support returns to mg. Being lower does not itself change mass or weight.

question.zh: 电梯一直上升，秤的读数为什么能先大后小？
question.en: Why can the reading first rise and then fall during one upward journey?

lead.zh: 跟住启动、匀速和制动；把速度方向与加速度方向分开。
lead.en: Follow start, cruise and braking, distinguishing velocity from acceleration.

principle.zh: N=m(g+a)取决于加速度；向上运动也能向下加速，产生偏小的读数。
principle.en: N=m(g+a) depends on acceleration. Upward motion can have downward acceleration and a reduced reading.

question.zh: 速度很大但保持匀速时，秤会一直偏大吗？
question.en: Does a high but constant speed keep the scale reading high?

explanation.zh: 匀速的加速度为零，读数恢复静止值。运动快慢与支持力大小不能直接对应。
explanation.en: Constant speed has zero acceleration, so the rest reading returns. Speed alone does not determine support force.

question.zh: 瓶子下落以后，为什么新水流停止，旧水滴却继续飞？
question.en: Why does falling stop the new jet while earlier droplets keep moving?

lead.zh: 先看通气水瓶的孔口压差，再跟住释放后的瓶、水柱和旧水滴。
lead.en: Start with the pressure difference in a vented bottle, then track bottle, water column and emitted drops.

principle.zh: 瓶与水共同自由落体，瓶内有效重力为零，持续静水压差消失；已喷出的水仍受地球引力。
principle.en: Shared free fall makes effective gravity zero inside the bottle, removing sustained pressure head. Emitted water still feels Earth’s gravity.

question.zh: 若没有新水流，是不是说明重力消失、旧水滴会停住？
question.en: Does the loss of a new jet mean gravity disappears and earlier drops stop?

explanation.zh: 不是。消失的是支持与持续压力作用；旧水滴仍按原水平速度和重力加速度运动，释放瞬态在本模型中省略。
explanation.en: No. Support and sustained pressure effects vanish; earlier drops keep their horizontal motion and gravitational acceleration. The release transient is omitted.
